independence_statement: Independent blind visual reading. The only reading inputs were the assigned conventions, scan029 boxes TSV, scan029 source JPG and crops I made directly from that JPG. No witness, edition, first transcription, other reader crop, note, proposal or comparison was opened or consulted. No OCR, text recognition, external research or TeX compilation was used. All readings, including doubts and editorial-state decisions, were made from the displayed images.
crop_method: Each exact supplied box was independently cropped with Pillow, enlarged to 3000 pixels wide using LANCZOS resampling, and autocontrasted. No rotation was needed. Supplemental context/detail crops used the same method, at 3000 pixels or 2500 pixels wide as recorded below. No text was obtained programmatically.

boxes.visible_stroke_evidence: The first numeral has a rounded upper hook, diagonal descent, and extended horizontal foot; the second has two joined loops. Both are at the head of the page: 28.

Several heavy horizontal strokes cancel the upper word. A capital A, tall loop after it, lower rounded loops, and a final s-like turn remain; Alors is a doubtful reading because the medial ink is covered. The lower replacement has a clear capital A, dotted i, n arch, s loop and final dotted i: Ainsi.

The heading has a single long underline. Inf ends in a long descending f. The relation consists of two separate left angles. The quoted noun has the descending f of figure, then an i and crossed t followed by the surviving section/tion strokes of intersection. The horizontal stroke through the first t is treated as its cross-stroke, not as a word cancellation. The brown irregular vertical mark before l'appelle differs in colour and edge texture from pen strokes and is not transcribed as a deleted word.

An interlinear en is followed by a descending g form, an acute mark and compressed low connections ending in a tall terminal stroke. A curved insertion leader connects the phrase with the gap before la figure.

Attention begins with a heavily retraced capital A. The long thin line is below the bodies of n'est pas and ends at pas, so it is read as an underline. The higher en général and curved leader are the insertion before la figure; the baseline la and long descending f of figure remain uncancelled.

A heavy horizontal deletion covers almost every medial letter. At the left there is a small loop with a short downstroke and an isolated upper mark; a high triangular ascender survives near the centre and a round right-facing turn survives at the right. quand is only a low-confidence candidate, not a secure decipherment.

The first word has a small open loop followed by low connected arches, read car. The next sign is an a-like body with a raised stroke. The last word has two deep p-like downstrokes, followed by a high loop and long low ending, read supposer.

F and G are separated by a comma. The inclusion is a curved open C-like sign, without an equality bar. The following P has a long descending stem and triangular bowl. A small separate low mark after the L inside the first parentheses leaves L versus L_1 uncertain. The final G, inclusion sign, and P(L) are all crossed by two long horizontal deletion strokes; the entire formula is retained inside the deletion.

The upper line begins with a capital D and the low connected strokes of Donc, followed by la bonne. The long central word has the distinctive t strokes and final tion sequence of intersection. The lower line shows la, F dot G and a separate stop; En begins with a capital E, fait has a long f and a crossed terminal t, and ça marche follows.

The left operator is a large pointed wedge between vertical modulus bars, with i in I beneath it and F_i to its right. The right operator is rounded like an intersection, also with i in I below, followed by a separately barred F_i. The equality has two short parallel strokes; a terminal dot is visible.

An initial s-like downstroke is followed by an apostrophe, a low oval a, paired descending p strokes, and looped/low connecting strokes terminating in a. Read s'appellera; no strike-through is visible.

A single horizontal line runs through the full phrase. The first item has the tall loop and low return of la. The next has a clear initial p descender, an i dot, obscured medial low strokes, and a tall t-like ending with an acute mark. propriété remains doubtful because its middle is masked.

The cancellation is the same left-hand phrase as in S029-12. The continuation rises sharply to the right: une has three low connected arches, followed by propriété with two descending p forms and a tall t, then de. A larger independent context crop was inspected to see the continuation whose ascenders lie above this horizontal box.

Two opening quotation strokes precede co, followed by a visible short hyphen. The next word has a looped d, dotted i, low r/e/c sequence and high crossed t, ending ion. One long line underlines the term. The raised pair at the upper right serves as the closing quotation mark, followed by a separate period.

Multiple long diagonal cancellation strokes cross all three lines, so the complete block is enclosed in deleted. Proposition is separately underlined. The first relation has a curved upper component and two low curved strokes; leq/preceq remains uncertain. An additional local horizontal erasure follows the first F; the proposed G' leq G is a doubtful complete formula, with only a crescent, low angular remnants and a terminal loop surviving. The later relation has a leftward upper angle and separate curved lower bar. The parenthesis begins Immédiat and ends in a word with an s-like angle, low u-like stroke, a descender and tall terminal t, tentatively surprenant. The short preceding word is uncertain. Subdivision has a capital S, a low u, tall b and looped d, then dotted i/v/i/s/i/on. The final line has underlined s'achète, par, un, and the two long f strokes of raffinement.

The first line is included in the larger diagonal block deletion. A short prime follows the first F. The first relation is overwritten/curved and is left doubtful between leq and preceq. A separate horizontal cancellation covers the material after that F; G' leq G is only a tentative complete formula. The later long diagonal passing beside the prime is a block-cancellation stroke, not a second prime. A small dot separates F' and G; the final F and G are likewise separated by a dot.

The left parenthesis and capital I are crossed by a diagonal deletion line. Immédiat has a visible acute mark, looped d, dotted i and high final t. After the comma is a short low connected word read tentatively un or mais. The final word has an initial angular s, low u-like connector, descender and a clear tall terminal t; surprenant remains tentative. The right parenthesis is followed by two vertically separated dots, read as a colon.
A diagonal block-cancellation stroke cuts the beginning, but the remaining p bowl and low a/r connection are visible. The word is par, included in the cancelled bottom paragraph.

At the left are s and a raised apostrophe. A low a is followed by the open c, tall looped h, low e-like connection and final tall crossed t with a low terminal e. The whole word is underlined; the diagonal line belongs to the cancellation of the full paragraph. Read s'achète, preserving both underline and deletion.

limitations: Low-confidence erased ink is retained as a visibly marked candidate. In particular, the short cancellation S029-06 and the local erased formula inside S029-15/S029-16 require adjudication; the parenthetical phrase S029-17 is also uncertain. The metadata kind column was not treated as proof that a visible line is a deletion.
